title: Track customer management measures
goal: The venture knows what a customer is worth over their life, how its customer revenue is trending and how many customers it keeps, every number counted from its own records and written where the next run can compare it.

steps.do: For each customer segment work out the revenue a customer brings over the time they stay and subtract the cost to serve them, show the arithmetic and the inputs, and write the figure on each customer record with the date counted.
Count customer revenue by period from the records, say which customers grew, which shrank and which stopped, and report the trend with the periods compared and the records counted.

Count how many customers the venture had at the start of each period, how many it kept and how many left, work out the retention and attrition rates, and name the reason each departure is recorded with.

Put the lifetime value, the trend and the retention rate beside the cost of winning a customer from the spend records, say which segment the venture actually makes money on, and name the number most likely to be wrong.
Propose what the numbers say to change, which segment to serve more, which to stop pursuing and which customer to speak to before they leave, each with the count behind it and the smallest next step.
Add each count to the goal or open decision it bears on, and bring the founder as a decision any change to which segment the venture serves.

done_criteria.check: Does every customer number written this run show its arithmetic, name the records counted and carry the date it was counted, so the next run can compare it?
